title: Constructible representation of an $H^1$ class

proof.text: *The setting.* $X=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$ is covered by the two affine opens $D_+(T_0)_S,D_+(T_1)_S$ [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] (a),(c), so it is quasi-compact; it is proper over the affine $S$ [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], hence separated, hence quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The same two lemmas with $s=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ in place of $S$ show that $X_0=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};s)$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2),(3) the inverse image $i^{-1}:\Mod(X_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\to\Mod(X_{0,\Et},\mathbf F_r)$ is an additive functor whose composite with the forgetful functor to abelian sheaves is the abelian inverse image of the underlying abelian sheaf (naturally in the sheaf); all groups $H^1$ below are those of underlying abelian sheaves.

source.place: Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover), etale-cohomology.tex line 16164, proof, first sentence 'Observe that X is a separated scheme which can be covered by 2 affine opens'; quasi-compactness of X and X_0 is what Lemmas 03SA and 03Q5 need

proof.text: *$I$ as a colimit of constructible sheaves (Stacks 03SA).* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaf-colimit-constructible] for the qcqs scheme $X$ (Step 1) and $\Lambda=\mathbf F_r$, there are a small filtered category $\mathcal A$, a diagram $\alpha\mapsto F_\alpha$ of constructible sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ and morphisms $a_\alpha:F_\alpha\to I$ in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)$ making $(I,(a_\alpha))$ a colimit of the diagram.

source.place: Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover), etale-cohomology.tex line 16164, proof, second paragraph, 'By Lemmas 03SA (lemma-torsion-colimit-constructible) and 03Q5 (lemma-colimit) we can find a map F -> I with F a constructible sheaf of Z/lZ-modules'

proof.text: *$\xi$ comes from some $F_\alpha$ (Stacks 03Q5).* The forgetful functor $\Mod(X_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\to\Ab(X_{\Et})$ preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] (2), so the underlying abelian sheaves form a colimit cocone $(I,(a_\alpha))$ in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$; the abelian inverse image $i^{-1}$ preserves all small colimits [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits], so $(i^{-1}I,(i^{-1}a_\alpha))$ is a colimit cocone of the filtered diagram $\alpha\mapsto i^{-1}F_\alpha$ in $\Ab(X_{0,\Et})$, and by Step 1 these are the underlying abelian sheaves and maps of the module inverse images. Since $X_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit] (with $q=1$) says that the canonical map $\varinjlim_\alpha H^1(X_0,i^{-1}F_\alpha)\to H^1(X_0,i^{-1}I)$, induced by the maps $H^1(i^{-1}a_\alpha)$, is bijective. Every element of a filtered colimit of abelian groups is the image of an element at some stage [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]; hence there are $\alpha\in\mathcal A$ and $\zeta\in H^1(X_0,i^{-1}F_\alpha)$ with $H^1(i^{-1}a_\alpha)(\zeta)=\xi$. Put $F=F_\alpha$, $a=a_\alpha:F\to I$.

source.place: Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover), etale-cohomology.tex line 16164, proof, second paragraph, '... and xi coming from an element zeta of H^1(X_0, F|_{X_0})' (Lemma 03Q5 on the qcqs X_0, with restriction to X_0 commuting with colimits)

proof.text: *Embedding into finite pushforwards (Stacks 09Z7).* $F$ is a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on the qcqs scheme $X$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-pushforward-embedding] with $\Lambda=\mathbf F_r$ there are $n\ge0$, finite morphisms $h_j:V_j\to X$ locally of finite presentation and finite $\mathbf F_r$-modules $M_j$ ($j=1,\dots,n$), and a monomorphism $\iota:F\hookrightarrow E=\bigoplus_{j=1}^nE_j$, $E_j=(h_j)_*\underline{M_j}$, in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)$. Let $\epsilon_j:E_j\to E$ and $\pi_j:E\to E_j$ be the injections and projections of the biproduct, so that $\sum_j\epsilon_j\pi_j=\mathrm{id}_E$ [def-weil-additive-category].

source.place: Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover), etale-cohomology.tex line 16164, proof, third paragraph, 'By Lemma 09Z7 (lemma-constructible-maps-into-constant-general) and the remarks above we may assume F is of the form f_*M where M is a finite Z/lZ-module and f: Y -> X is a finite morphism of finite presentation'

proof.text: *Extending across $\iota$ by injectivity.* $I$ is injective in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)$ and $\iota$ is a monomorphism, so $\operatorname{Hom}(E,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}(F,I)$, $\psi\mapsto\psi\circ\iota$, is surjective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]: there is $\psi:E\to I$ with $\psi\circ\iota=a$. Put $\psi_j=\psi\circ\epsilon_j:(h_j)_*\underline{M_j}\to I$, a morphism of sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules; then $\psi=\psi\circ\sum_j\epsilon_j\pi_j=\sum_j\psi_j\circ\pi_j$.

source.place: Lemma 0A5H (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-fibre-by-finite-cover), etale-cohomology.tex line 16164, proof, second paragraph, 'Since I is injective we can extend the given map F -> I to a map F' -> I ... if F = F_1 + F_2 is a direct sum, then we may replace F by F_i'

proof.text:
*The classes $x_j$.* Put $\zeta'=H^1(i^{-1}\iota)(\zeta)\in H^1(X_0,i^{-1}E)$ and $x_j=H^1(i^{-1}\pi_j)(\zeta')\in H^1(X_0,i^{-1}(h_j)_*\underline{M_j})$. The map $\varphi\mapsto H^1(\varphi)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] is additive and functorial: if $\tilde\varphi,\tilde\varphi'$ are lifts of $\varphi,\varphi'$ to K-injective resolutions, then $\tilde\varphi+\tilde\varphi'$ lifts $\varphi+\varphi'$ and $\tilde\varphi'\circ\tilde\varphi$ lifts $\varphi'\circ\varphi$, and $\mathcal H^1(\Gamma(X_0,-))$ is additive and functorial on morphisms of complexes; by independence of the lift, $H^1(\varphi+\varphi')=H^1(\varphi)+H^1(\varphi')$ and $H^1(\varphi'\circ\varphi)=H^1(\varphi')\circ H^1(\varphi)$. The functor $i^{-1}$ on sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules is additive (Step 1). Hence, using Step 5,
$$\sum_jH^1(i^{-1}\psi_j)(x_j)=\sum_jH^1(i^{-1}(\psi_j\pi_j))(\zeta')=H^1\Bigl(i^{-1}\sum_j\psi_j\pi_j\Bigr)(\zeta')=H^1(i^{-1}\psi)(\zeta')=H^1(i^{-1}(\psi\iota))(\zeta)=H^1(i^{-1}a)(\zeta)=\xi$$
by Step 3. This gives $n$, $h_j$, $M_j$, $\psi_j$ and $x_j$ as in the statement.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For an injective sheaf $I$ of $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules on $\mathbf P^1_A$,
every class
$c\in H^1(X_0,I_0)$ admits finite $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules $M_i$, finite finitely presented
morphisms $h_i:V_i\to X$, and a map
$\bigoplus_i(h_i)_*\underline{M_i}\to I$ such that $c$ is the image of a
tuple of classes in
$\bigoplus_iH^1(X_0,(h_i)_*\underline{M_i}|_{X_0})$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
View $c$ as the isomorphism class of an $I_0$-torsor. It is trivial on an
etale cover; quasi-compactness of $X_0$ selects finitely many members
$U_a\to X_0$. Choosing local origins gives a Cech cocycle
$z=(z_{ab})$ with

$$
z_{ab}\in I_0(U_a\times_{X_0}U_b),\qquad
z_{bc}-z_{ac}+z_{ab}=0
$$

on every triple overlap. There are finitely many sections and equations.
Constructible approximation therefore supplies a constructible sheaf $F$, a
map $\alpha:F\to I$, and lifts $\widetilde z_{ab}\in F_0(U_{ab})$
satisfying the same equations and mapping to $z_{ab}$.

The finite-pushforward lemma gives a monomorphism
$\iota:F\hookrightarrow F'=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r(h_i)_*\underline{M_i}$.
Injectivity of $I$ extends $\alpha$ across $\iota$ to a map
$\psi:F'\to I$. The sheaf square and the three relevant terms of the Cech
complex form the commuting three-row diagram

$$
\begin{CD}
F @>{\iota}>> F' @>>> \operatorname{coker}(\iota)\\
@V{\alpha}VV @V{\psi}VV @VVV\\
I @= I @>>> 0\\[2pt]
@VVV @VVV @VVV\\
\prod_a I_0(U_a) @>{d^0}>>
\prod_{a,b} I_0(U_{ab}) @>{d^1}>>
\prod_{a,b,c} I_0(U_{abc}).
\end{CD}
$$

Here the bottom vertical maps mean restriction followed by the indicated
Cech cochain inclusion; commutativity in degrees $0,1,2$ follows from
functoriality of restriction. The cocycle $\iota(\widetilde z)$ defines
$c'\in H^1(X_0,F'_0)$ and $\psi_0(c')=c$.

Finite direct sums commute with $H^1$, while exact finite direct image and
Leray give

$$
H^1(X_0,F'_0)=
\bigoplus_{i=1}^rH^1(X_0,(h_i)_*\underline{M_i}|_{X_0})
=\bigoplus_{i=1}^rH^1((V_i)_0,\underline{M_i}).
$$

Thus $c'$ is the required finite tuple, and the displayed map $F'\to I$
sends that tuple to the original class.
